description: issue #768: the POSITIVE complement of the `input-prompt-*-rejected` fixtures, and the half that makes them discriminating rather than vacuous. The program is byte-identical to `input-prompt-number-rejected` except that the prompt is quoted — `input "42"` versus `input 42` — so the two prompts display the same two characters while the pair demands OPPOSITE verdicts on them. A word prompt is accepted (`spec/interaction-events.md:181`: "**Args:** one prompt, which MUST be a `word`"): the read runs, emits its `primitive` event named `input` after the answer is in hand, and reports the scripted answer, which `print` then prints. That identical-text/opposite-verdict property is what the pair buys. No classifier that looks only at the prompt's PRINTED FORM can satisfy both members — whichever way it decides on `42`, it fails one of them: accepting numerals fails `input-prompt-number-rejected`, rejecting them fails HERE. Separately, an implementation that rejected EVERY prompt would pass all three negatives and fail HERE. Neither member alone catches both classes. This is also why `params.expected` is `"word"` and not `"text"`: the constraint is a type, and OpenLogo already spells that type as `word` (`word "Question" 3` raises `ol-type` with `expected: "word"`).
